doc.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023

title: 'A Love Supreme' appearing at the end of the track
summary: Coltrane's tune entered the recording unplanned and they kept it.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Wonderful. And I did hear “A Love Supreme” as that tune faded out. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
I don’t know where that came from.
I was going to ask where did that come from.

I don’t know where that came from. We were just in the tune you know, and all that had happened, you know the track, right, so it’s like seven minutes or nine minutes already and then out of — and then when I did it I said, “Oh we’ll be out by then.” We listened to the playback and I said, “Oh we’ll be faded by then” you know the tune won’t last that long, we won’t do that. And there it was, we kept it, because it was all part of that thing. And I think that was the most beautiful part of it all, that the modern ancestors and the whole idea of what I was doing, somehow this John Coltrane entered the recording session, you know whoa. But that’s the beautiful, spiritual part of what we do.
